eyebrow: Python for Data Engineers · Chapter 3, Lesson 17
subtitle: Real HTTP calls against GitHub's live, public API.

code:
import requests

response = requests.get("https://api.github.com/repos/pandas-dev/pandas")
print(response.status_code)

data = response.json()
print(data["full_name"])
print(data["description"])
print(data["stargazers_count"])
print(data["language"])
caption: requests.get() sends the HTTP request; .json() parses the response body into a Python dict, just like json.loads().

eyebrow: Checking status_code before trusting the data
caption: A typo'd URL doesn't raise an exception on its own -- GitHub just returns a 404 with a normal JSON body.
raise_for_status() raises requests.HTTPError on 4xx/5xx — combined with Lesson 16's try/except, it's a pattern you'll reuse constantly.

code:
response = requests.get(
    "https://api.github.com/repos/pandas-dev/pandas/contributors"
)
contributors = response.json()

print(len(contributors))
print(contributors[0]["login"])
print(contributors[0]["contributions"])
caption: GitHub only returns the first 30 contributors per page by default — exactly the limit Lesson 18 covers next.

subtitle: Walking through every page without getting rate-limited.
